notable steps to provide refugee education access. That is a real inclusion signal, even though resources were still inadequate.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.8"]},{"title":"Minister: Labor ministry has strategy to empower women","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"2024-03-23","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/minister-labor-ministry-has-strategy-to-empower-women/","summary":"The labor ministry said women’s economic empowerment and equal labor-market participation were top priorities at Sisi’s direction, with training programs and a gender-equality unit.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.8"]},{"title":"Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-05-13","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/","summary":"Amnesty documented arrests of people criticizing prices, workers striking for the minimum wage, and protesters blaming Sisi for “starving” the poor. That suggests the regime treated welfare complaints as threats to be suppressed, not as core feedback to govern by.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.9","5B.7"]},{"title":"Egypt: More than 100 arbitrarily detained over calls for anti-government protests","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-07-18","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/","summary":"Amnesty said 119 people were detained after calls for protests over price hikes and power cuts. This is strong evidence that economic pain triggered coercion rather than a welfare-first response.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.9","5B.7"]},{"title":"Egypt: Education Restricted for Refugees","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-12-02","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/egypt-education-restricted-for-refugees","summary":"HRW found tens of thousands of refugee and asylum-seeking children out of school because of residency requirements, costs, discrimination, and lack of free public education. That undercuts a claim of broad human-welfare concern across vulnerable groups.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.8"]},{"title":"Egypt: Authorities Must End Campaign of Mass Arrests and Forced Returns of Sudanese Refugees","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-06-19","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/egypt-authorities-must-end-campaign-of-mass-arrests-and-forced-returns-of-sudanese-refugees/","summary":"Amnesty documented mass arrests, cruel detention conditions, and forced returns of Sudanese refugees without asylum access. This is strong contrary evidence for welfare across vulnerable groups.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.8"]},{"title":"Human Rights Watch World Report 2024: Egypt","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/egypt","summary":"HRW reported harsh prison conditions, denied family and lawyer access, and refusal to reopen the economist Aymad Hadhoud case. That points to welfare being secondary to control when vulnerable people were politically inconvenient.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.9","5B.7"]},{"title":"National Human Rights Strategy","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"2024","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/strategies/national-human-rights-strategy/","summary":"The state’s own human-rights messaging includes anti-violence and anti-extortion campaigns, but it is still official framing rather than independent proof that welfare consistently outweighed regime survival.","question_ids":["6B.1","5B.9"]}]}
